audit_status.source_base: Greek 1 Timothy text tradition, draft aligned to public-domain comparison layer later
audit_status.review_note: Compact draft reviewed for household care, widows, elders, accusations, impartiality, health note, visible/hidden works.

verses.restored: Do not rebuke an older man sharply, but encourage as father, younger men as siblings,

familiar.text: Rebuke not an elder, but intreat him as a father; and the younger men as brethren;

modern.text: Do not rebuke an older man, but appeal to him as to a father. Treat younger men as brothers,

original.text: Πρεσβυτέρῳ μὴ ἐπιπλήξῃς, ἀλλὰ παρακάλει ὡς πατέρα, νεωτέρους ὡς ἀδελφούς,

verses.restored: older women as mothers, younger women as sisters, in all purity.

familiar.text: The elder women as mothers; the younger as sisters, with all purity.

modern.text: older women as mothers, and younger women as sisters, with absolute purity. Honoring True Widows (Ruth 1:1–5)

original.text: πρεσβυτέρας ὡς μητέρας, νεωτέρας ὡς ἀδελφὰς ἐν πάσῃ ἁγνείᾳ.

verses.restored: Honor widows who are truly widows.

familiar.text: Honour widows that are widows indeed.

modern.text: Honor the widows who are truly widows.

original.text: Χήρας τίμα τὰς ὄντως χήρας.

verses.restored: But if any widow has children or grandchildren, let them first learn to practice reverence toward their own household and to give repayment to parents, for this is acceptable before the Divine.

familiar.text: But if any widow have children or nephews, let them learn first to shew piety at home, and to requite their parents: for that is good and acceptable before God.

modern.text: But if a widow has children or grandchildren, they must first learn to show godliness to their own family and repay their parents, for this is pleasing in the sight of God.

original.text: εἰ δέ τις χήρα τέκνα ἢ ἔκγονα ἔχει, μανθανέτωσαν πρῶτον τὸν ἴδιον οἶκον εὐσεβεῖν καὶ ἀμοιβὰς ἀποδιδόναι τοῖς προγόνοις, τοῦτο γάρ ἐστιν ἀπόδεκτον ἐνώπιον τοῦ θεοῦ.

verses.restored: Now the one truly a widow and left alone has hoped upon the Divine and remains in petitions and prayers night and day.

familiar.text: Now she that is a widow indeed, and desolate, trusteth in God, and continueth in supplications and prayers night and day.

modern.text: The widow who is truly in need and left all alone puts her hope in God and continues night and day in her petitions and prayers.

original.text: ἡ δὲ ὄντως χήρα καὶ μεμονωμένη ἤλπικεν ἐπὶ ⸀θεὸν καὶ προσμένει ταῖς δεήσεσιν καὶ ταῖς προσευχαῖς νυκτὸς καὶ ἡμέρας·

verses.restored: But the one living in indulgence has died while living.

familiar.text: But she that liveth in pleasure is dead while she liveth.

modern.text: But she who lives for pleasure is dead even while she is still alive.

original.text: ἡ δὲ σπαταλῶσα ζῶσα τέθνηκεν.

verses.restored: Command these things also, so that they may be above reproach.

familiar.text: And these things give in charge, that they may be blameless.

modern.text: Give these instructions to the believers, so that they will be above reproach.

original.text: καὶ ταῦτα παράγγελλε, ἵνα ἀνεπίλημπτοι ὦσιν·

verses.restored: But if anyone does not provide for one's own, and especially for household members, one has denied the trust and is worse than an untrusting one.

familiar.text: But if any provide not for his own, and specially for those of his own house, he hath denied the faith, and is worse than an infidel.

modern.text: If anyone does not provide for his own, and especially his own household, he has denied the faith and is worse than an unbeliever.

original.text: εἰ δέ τις τῶν ἰδίων καὶ ⸀μάλιστα οἰκείων οὐ ⸀προνοεῖ, τὴν πίστιν ἤρνηται καὶ ἔστιν ἀπίστου χείρων.

verses.restored: Let a widow be enrolled not less than sixty years old, having been wife of one husband,

familiar.text: Let not a widow be taken into the number under threescore years old, having been the wife of one man,

modern.text: A widow should be enrolled if she is at least sixty years old, the wife of one man,

original.text: Χήρα καταλεγέσθω μὴ ἔλαττον ἐτῶν ἑξήκοντα γεγονυῖα, ἑνὸς ἀνδρὸς γυνή,

verses.restored: being witnessed to in beautiful/good works: if she raised children, showed hospitality, washed feet of holy ones, helped pressured ones, followed every beautiful/good work.

familiar.text: Well reported of for good works; if she have brought up children, if she have lodged strangers, if she have washed the saints’ feet, if she have relieved the afflicted, if she have diligently followed every good work.

modern.text: and well known for good deeds such as bringing up children, entertaining strangers, washing the feet of the saints, imparting relief to the afflicted, and devoting herself to every good work.

original.text: ἐν ἔργοις καλοῖς μαρτυρουμένη, εἰ ἐτεκνοτρόφησεν, εἰ ἐξενοδόχησεν, εἰ ἁγίων πόδας ἔνιψεν, εἰ θλιβομένοις ἐπήρκεσεν, εἰ παντὶ ἔργῳ ἀγαθῷ ἐπηκολούθησεν.

verses.restored: But younger widows refuse/enroll not; for when desires draw them away from Messiah, they want to marry,

familiar.text: But the younger widows refuse: for when they have begun to wax wanton against Christ, they will marry;

modern.text: But refuse to enroll younger widows. For when their passions draw them away from Christ, they will want to marry,

original.text: νεωτέρας δὲ χήρας παραιτοῦ· ὅταν γὰρ καταστρηνιάσωσιν τοῦ Χριστοῦ, γαμεῖν θέλουσιν,

verses.restored: having judgment because they set aside the first trust/pledge.

familiar.text: Having damnation, because they have cast off their first faith.

modern.text: and thus will incur judgment because they are setting aside their first faith.

original.text: ἔχουσαι κρίμα ὅτι τὴν πρώτην πίστιν ἠθέτησαν·

verses.restored: And at the same time they also learn to be idle, going around houses, and not only idle but also gossiping and meddling, speaking things not necessary.

familiar.text: And withal they learn to be idle, wandering about from house to house; and not only idle, but tattlers also and busybodies, speaking things which they ought not.

modern.text: At the same time they will also learn to be idle, going from house to house and being not only idle, but also gossips and busybodies, discussing things they should not mention.

original.text: ἅμα δὲ καὶ ἀργαὶ μανθάνουσιν, περιερχόμεναι τὰς οἰκίας, οὐ μόνον δὲ ἀργαὶ ἀλλὰ καὶ φλύαροι καὶ περίεργοι, λαλοῦσαι τὰ μὴ δέοντα.

verses.restored: Therefore I desire younger widows to marry, bear children, manage households, give no starting point to the opposing one for reproach.

familiar.text: I will therefore that the younger women marry, bear children, guide the house, give none occasion to the adversary to speak reproachfully.

modern.text: So I advise the younger widows to marry, have children, and manage their households, denying the adversary occasion for slander.

original.text: βούλομαι οὖν νεωτέρας γαμεῖν, τεκνογονεῖν, οἰκοδεσποτεῖν, μηδεμίαν ἀφορμὴν διδόναι τῷ ἀντικειμένῳ λοιδορίας χάριν·

verses.restored: For already some turned aside after the adversarial one.

familiar.text: For some are already turned aside after Satan.

modern.text: For some have already turned aside to follow Satan.

original.text: ἤδη γάρ τινες ἐξετράπησαν ὀπίσω τοῦ Σατανᾶ.

verses.restored: If any trusting woman has widows, let her assist them, and let not the assembly be burdened, so that it may assist those truly widows.

familiar.text: If any man or woman that believeth have widows, let them relieve them, and let not the church be charged; that it may relieve them that are widows indeed.

modern.text: If any believing woman has dependent widows, she must assist them and not allow the church to be burdened, so that it can help the widows who are truly in need. Honoring Elders

original.text: εἴ ⸀τις πιστὴ ἔχει χήρας, ⸀ἐπαρκείτω αὐταῖς, καὶ μὴ βαρείσθω ἡ ἐκκλησία, ἵνα ταῖς ὄντως χήραις ἐπαρκέσῃ.

verses.restored: Let the elders leading beautifully/well be considered worthy of double honor, especially those laboring in word and teaching.

familiar.text: Let the elders that rule well be counted worthy of double honour, especially they who labour in the word and doctrine.

modern.text: Elders who lead effectively are worthy of double honor, especially those who work hard at preaching and teaching.

original.text: Οἱ καλῶς προεστῶτες πρεσβύτεροι διπλῆς τιμῆς ἀξιούσθωσαν, μάλιστα οἱ κοπιῶντες ἐν λόγῳ καὶ διδασκαλίᾳ·

verses.restored: For the Scripture says, You shall not muzzle an ox threshing, and, The worker is worthy of wages.

familiar.text: For the scripture saith, Thou shalt not muzzle the ox that treadeth out the corn. And, The labourer is worthy of his reward.

modern.text: For the Scripture says, “Do not muzzle an ox while it is treading out the grain,” and, “The worker is worthy of his wages.”

original.text: λέγει γὰρ ἡ γραφή· Βοῦν ἀλοῶντα οὐ φιμώσεις, καί· Ἄξιος ὁ ἐργάτης τοῦ μισθοῦ αὐτοῦ.

verses.restored: Do not receive an accusation against an elder except upon two or three witnesses.

familiar.text: Against an elder receive not an accusation, but before two or three witnesses.

modern.text: Do not entertain an accusation against an elder, except on the testimony of two or three witnesses.

original.text: κατὰ πρεσβυτέρου κατηγορίαν μὴ παραδέχου, ἐκτὸς εἰ μὴ ἐπὶ δύο ἢ τριῶν μαρτύρων·

verses.restored: Those sinning/misaligning, expose before all, so that the rest may have reverence.

familiar.text: Them that sin rebuke before all, that others also may fear.

modern.text: But those who persist in sin should be rebuked in front of everyone, so that the others will stand in fear of sin. A Charge to Timothy

original.text: ⸀τοὺς ἁμαρτάνοντας ἐνώπιον πάντων ἔλεγχε, ἵνα καὶ οἱ λοιποὶ φόβον ἔχωσιν.

verses.restored: I solemnly testify before the Divine and Messiah Jesus and the chosen messengers, that you guard these things without prejudgment, doing nothing according to partiality.

familiar.text: I charge thee before God, and the Lord Jesus Christ, and the elect angels, that thou observe these things without preferring one before another, doing nothing by partiality.

modern.text: I solemnly charge you before God and Christ Jesus and the elect angels to maintain these principles without bias, and to do nothing out of partiality.

original.text: διαμαρτύρομαι ἐνώπιον τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ ⸂Χριστοῦ Ἰησοῦ⸃ καὶ τῶν ἐκλεκτῶν ἀγγέλων, ἵνα ταῦτα φυλάξῃς χωρὶς προκρίματος, μηδὲν ποιῶν κατὰ πρόσκλισιν.

verses.restored: Lay hands quickly on no one, nor share in others' sins/misalignments; keep yourself pure.

familiar.text: Lay hands suddenly on no man, neither be partaker of other men’s sins: keep thyself pure.

modern.text: Do not be too quick in the laying on of hands and thereby share in the sins of others. Keep yourself pure.

original.text: χεῖρας ταχέως μηδενὶ ἐπιτίθει, μηδὲ κοινώνει ἁμαρτίαις ἀλλοτρίαις· σεαυτὸν ἁγνὸν τήρει.

verses.restored: No longer drink water only, but use a little wine because of your stomach and your frequent weaknesses.

familiar.text: Drink no longer water, but use a little wine for thy stomach’s sake and thine often infirmities.

modern.text: Stop drinking only water and use a little wine instead, because of your stomach and your frequent ailments.

original.text: μηκέτι ὑδροπότει, ἀλλὰ οἴνῳ ὀλίγῳ χρῶ διὰ τὸν ⸀στόμαχον καὶ τὰς πυκνάς σου ἀσθενείας.

verses.restored: The sins/misalignments of some humans are evident beforehand, going before into judgment, but for others they also follow after.

familiar.text: Some men’s sins are open beforehand, going before to judgment; and some men they follow after.

modern.text: The sins of some men are obvious, going ahead of them to judgment; but the sins of others do not surface until later.

original.text: Τινῶν ἀνθρώπων αἱ ἁμαρτίαι πρόδηλοί εἰσιν, προάγουσαι εἰς κρίσιν, τισὶν δὲ καὶ ἐπακολουθοῦσιν·

verses.restored: Likewise also the beautiful/good works are evident beforehand, and those otherwise cannot be hidden.

familiar.text: Likewise also the good works of some are manifest beforehand; and they that are otherwise cannot be hid.

modern.text: In the same way, good deeds are obvious, and even the ones that are inconspicuous cannot remain hidden.

original.text: ὡσαύτως καὶ τὰ ⸂ἔργα τὰ καλὰ⸃ ⸀πρόδηλα, καὶ τὰ ἄλλως ἔχοντα κρυβῆναι οὐ δύνανται.

translation_notes: Widow care is economic and communal; do not reduce it to moral policing. The chapter distinguishes family responsibility and assembly responsibility.
Accusation and discipline rules require witness, impartiality, and caution against hasty authorization.
The wine/stomach verse is a practical health note, not a spirituality test.
